newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end at year peak with Aegon the star.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end at year peak with Aegon the star.

text.p: Dutch shares surged in the afternoon to close at a record high on the year's last day of trading with insurer Aegon the market's star stock.
The AEX index of blue chip stocks ended up 9.15 points to 648.24, the highest close of the year, having shortly before reached a new intra-day peak of 648.32.
The surge left the index 162.89 points, or 33.6 percent, higher than at the end of 1995.
Monday's main thrust came from the insurer Aegon with its announcement that it is to acquire the insurance activities of Providian Corp of the United States, a deal worth $3.5 billion.

The takeover is the biggest U.S. acquisition by a Dutch company this year and is expected to be completed by the middle of 1997. The deal, involving a tax-free share swap, will make Aegon one of the top three European insurance players.
Aegon shares rose 10.90 guilders, or 11.0 percent, to 110.10.
"It's unbelievable. Aegon (accounts for) more than 50 percent of the AEX gain," one trader said.
Aegon's sharp gains slightly masked continued bullish sentiment in the market as a whole. Traders said they expected the strength to continue through January.
"Everybody is buying, no-one is selling for the time being," one trader said.
Positive news also lifted software firm Baan Company, up 2.10 guilders to 60.80. The company recently said that its 1997 performance would be as healthy as that of 1996.
A little more mystifying was the strength of brewer Heineken which rose 2.60 guilders to 305.80. One trader said it was perhaps a reaction to the relative underperformance of the stock this year.
One disappointment was Philips which ended unchanged at 70.00 guilders.
The stock failed to firm after a statement from Grundig, its German electronics subsidiary. Grundig said it expected to make a loss in 1997 despite improvements.
